input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us (the Customer) for late payment at fifteen percent of annual Fees per week of delay — compounding to more than the annual contract value within seven weeks and triggered by a minor administrative breach. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (which contemplates only a capped early-termination fee, not an open-ended late-payment penalty). No early-termination fee or other Customer-payable liquidated amount appears elsewhere: Sections 9.4 and 10.2 require only accrued Fees plus refunds of prepayments, which is favourable to us. We propose the preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us — substituting standard interest on undisputed overdue amounts and preserving the good-faith withholding right in Section 7.3.

proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment with modest late-payment interest on undisputed sums
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay is a penalty far exceeding any credible loss. We have replaced it with standard interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving the dispute protections in Section 7.3.

ops.newText: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice remains unpaid after its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at one percent per month (or the lower maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law) from the due date until payment. Customer is not liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar charge in respect of late payment, and amounts withheld under Section 7.3 do not accrue interest unless ultimately found due.
